inspectedText: The heritage teaching booklet prints an attributed transcription of William Wells Brown's letter dated January4,1849, published in The Liberator January12,1849. The passage reports Ellen in men's clothing as master, William as servant, inability to read/write, and binding her right hand to avoid signing. This is a useful near-contemporary source lead separate in time from the 1860 memoir, but the original newspaper scan was not inspected. Brown was an abolitionist associate, not a witness to the journey; independent information provenance remains uncertain. The booklet's adjacent biography has discrepant death/birth detail and simplified marriage/general claims, which are not relied on. Screenshot attempts failed with cache miss; inspection was PDF text extraction only.
sourceQualityRationale: Modern educational transcription of a potentially valuable contemporaneous report. Provisionally supports chronology of the core account but requires original-scan authentication before final evidence review; no count of fully independent witnesses.
